findings.title: Two error codes emitted by the new supplier endpoints are absent from the /api/v1/meta/error-codes registry (indirection factory defeats the AST scan)
findings.why_it_matters: The new PUT /api/v1/equipment/{id}/actual-data and POST .../actual-data/confirm return 422 envelopes whose `code` is `ACTUAL_DATA_VALIDATION` or `DEVIATION_BLOCKS_CONFIRMATION` (the test suite at tests/api/v1/test_supplier_actual_data_api.py:156 asserts the former is emitted). But the registry endpoint the project treats as the authority for error codes -- CLAUDE.md: '字段/枚举/权限/错误码以 OpenAPI + meta API 为准' -- does not list either of them. A client that fetches /api/v1/meta/error-codes to build its code -> UI-behaviour map (each entry carries `ui_behavior`) finds no entry, so the two codes the new endpoints actually emit are untranslatable and fall through to whatever the client's default branch does. I ran the project's own scanner (`app/services/meta_service.py::_scan_error_codes`) over `app/` and it registers 115 codes; neither new code is among them.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/actual_data_service.py:27-30 -- `def _validation_error(message: str) -> PcsError:` / `return PcsError(` / `code="ACTUAL_DATA_VALIDATION", message=message, status=422` / `)` -- the code is produced by a *returned* PcsError, never by a `raise PcsError(...)` statement.

pcs-backend/app/services/meta_service.py:311 -- `if not (isinstance(cf, ast.Name) and cf.id == "PcsError"):` -- the scanner only matches a Raise node whose call target is literally the name `PcsError`; `raise _validation_error(...)` and `raise _error(...)` do not match, so the code constant is never visited.

pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/confirmation_service.py:40-41 -- `def _error(code: str, message: str, status: int = 422) -> PcsError:` / `return PcsError(code=code, message=message, status=status)` -- same indirection, used at confirmation_service.py:60 and :67 for `DEVIATION_BLOCKS_CONFIRMATION`.

Executed the project's scanner logic verbatim over `app/`: `ACTUAL_DATA_VALIDATION -> *** NOT REGISTERED IN META ***`, `DEVIATION_BLOCKS_CONFIRMATION -> *** NOT REGISTERED IN META ***`, `ACTUAL_DATA_LOCKED -> ['app/services/supplier/actual_data_service.py:93']`, total registered codes: 115.

Convention check: `grep -c 'raise PcsError'` finds 160 direct `raise PcsError(` sites across 28 files under app/services/. The two new supplier services are the only ones in the codebase that route codes through a factory function.

pcs-backend/tests/api/v1/test_supplier_actual_data_api.py:156 -- `assert resp.json()["code"] == "ACTUAL_DATA_VALIDATION"` -- confirms the unregistered code is part of the emitted public contract, not dead code.
findings.suggested_fix: Assumption: the meta registry's AST scan is the intended single source of error-code truth and the factory indirection is incidental, not a deliberate decision to exclude these codes. Two defensible fixes; I recommend the first because it is local to this branch and does not change a shared scanner. (1) Local: inline the raise at each of the 8 `_validation_error` / `_error` call sites so each carries a literal `raise PcsError(code="ACTUAL_DATA_VALIDATION", ...)` that the existing scanner picks up -- matches the 160-site convention, costs a little repetition. (2) Alternative: teach `_scan_error_codes` to also walk `return PcsError(code=<Constant>)` nodes, which fixes the class of bug but touches a shared, pre-existing component and would need its own regression test. Either way, verify by re-running the scanner and confirming both codes appear, then add a test asserting the new codes are present in the /api/v1/meta/error-codes response.

findings.title: Hyrum's Law: all five supplier endpoints ship at /api/v1/equipment/... but the frozen SPEC API table documents all five under /api/v1/equipment-list/..., with no SPEC revision registered
findings.file: spec/工艺专用综合计算软件需求规格说明书 Web版 P7.md
findings.why_it_matters: The SPEC's public API table lists the whole 供应商数据 surface under the `/api/v1/equipment-list/` prefix, and the implementation publishes every one of those paths under `/api/v1/equipment/`. A client (or the next implementer, or a contract test) written against the SPEC table sends a request that 404s -- and a 404 here is indistinguishable from "equipment does not exist", because `_load_equipment` deliberately collapses not-found and no-access into the same response. The project's own rule resolves the conflict in favour of OpenAPI but requires the SPEC revision to be registered; `git diff <base> -- spec/` is empty, so the authoritative document and the shipped contract now disagree with no record of the ruling. The SPEC additionally lists `POST /api/v1/equipment-list/{equipment_id}/actual-data/import` (Excel batch import) which is deliberately not implemented at all, and is likewise unregistered.
evidence: spec/工艺专用综合计算软件需求规格说明书 Web版 P7.md:145 -- `GET /api/v1/equipment-list/{equipment_id}/deviation-report	获取偏差报告`

spec/工艺专用综合计算软件需求规格说明书 Web版 P7.md:142-146 -- the same table's other four entries: `POST /api/v1/equipment-list/{equipment_id}/actual-data	录入实际数据`, `POST /api/v1/equipment-list/{equipment_id}/actual-data/import	Excel批量导入`, `POST /api/v1/equipment-list/{equipment_id}/actual-data/confirm	确认实际数据`, `POST /api/v1/equipment-list/{equipment_id}/actual-data/check	校核实际数据`
pcs-backend/app/api/v1/supplier.py:58 -- `router = APIRouter(prefix="/equipment", tags=["supplier"])` -- the only line in the file that moves the surface off the documented prefix.

pcs-backend/app/api/v1/equip_list.py:39 -- `router = APIRouter(prefix="/equipment-list", tags=["equipment-list"])` -- the SPEC's prefix is a real, separately-mounted router; the new paths are not reachable under it.
`git diff 3e5ae902945e19274f5be410f0eed31eb48a7627 -- spec/` returns empty: the SPEC was not revised in this branch, so no ruling is registered in the authoritative document.

Routing safety verified: of 37 `APIRouter(prefix=...)` declarations under app/api/v1/, `/equipment` is declared exactly once, so the two prefixes do not collide or shadow for the same equipment_id -- the divergence is a documentation/contract mismatch, not a live routing ambiguity.

No shipped consumer yet: `grep -rn 'deviation-report\|actual-data' pcs-frontend/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` (excluding generated types/api.d.ts) returns nothing, so no client is currently broken -- the exposure is to the next consumer and to the next implementer.
findings.suggested_fix: Assumption: `/api/v1/equipment/` is the intended final path (the S4-1/S4-2 shared-router-prefix ruling is recorded in docs/sprint4-plan-2026-10-05.md and .superpowers/sdd/sprint4-plan-2026-10-05/progress.md:93, and it is a reasonable one), and the SPEC is the artifact that must catch up. Do not move the code back. Register the revision in the SPEC API table: change the 供应商数据 block's five paths to the `/api/v1/equipment/` prefix, mark the `actual-data/import` row as deliberately not implemented under the S4-1 manual-UI ruling (or delete the row), and add the SPEC-ADD entry the project's other divergences use (e.g. the existing `SPEC-ADD-001 V1.13 §3.4.2` markers in the same file) so the ruling is traceable from the code. If instead the SPEC prefix is considered non-negotiable, the change is a one-line prefix swap in supplier.py plus regenerating the OpenAPI artifacts -- but that contradicts the recorded ruling, so it needs an explicit decision first.

findings.title: Unbounded free-form parameter names on a public write surface whose read surface is a closed rule set -- nothing in the contract tells a client which keys are judgeable
findings.why_it_matters: The write side accepts any 1-100 character string as a parameter name and stores it verbatim as a key of the public `actual_data_json` object; the read side interprets those keys against a closed, fixed rule set and returns `UNVERDICTABLE` for every key it does not recognise. Nothing in the request schema, the response schema, or the endpoint docs states the set of meaningful keys, so a client can successfully write data that is permanently unjudgeable -- the write returns 200 with the offending value echoed back, and the failure only surfaces later as a `UNVERDICTABLE` row and `can_confirm: false`. Because the endpoint docstring at supplier.py:153-154 already records that `design_parameters_json` has no writer (so production reports are entirely `UNVERDICTABLE` and `can_confirm` is effectively always false), the write surface currently has no path to a judged report at all. Compounding this, the response type is a bare `dict`, which the generator emits as `{[key: string]: unknown} | null` -- the client gets no per-value typing and must re-narrow `unknown` itself.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/schemas/supplier.py:22 -- `name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100, description="参数名")` -- any string is a legal key; there is no allow-list, no enum, and no cross-reference to the engine's rule set.

pcs-backend/app/schemas/supplier.py:44 -- `actual_data_json: dict | None = None` -- the public response type is an untyped map; the generated `pcs-frontend/src/types/api.d.ts:5250-5252` renders it as `actual_data_json?: { [key: string]: unknown; } | null;`.

pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/deviation_report.py:93-100 -- `if rule is None:` / `rows.append(DeviationRow(parameter=name, design_value=design_value, actual_value=actual_value, unit=unit, deviation_pct=None, verdict=UNVERDICTABLE, note="无判定规则（SPEC §3.2.4(2) 以泵为例）", spec_ref="",))` -- an unrecognised key is accepted into the report rather than rejected at write time.

pcs-backend/app/api/v1/supplier.py:153-155 -- `⚠️ 已知缺口：`design_parameters_json` 目前无写入方，故生产路径上全部行 都会落「缺设计值（不可判）」` -- the endpoint documents that no production row can currently be judged, so the accepted-but-unusable write surface is the whole surface today.

pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/actual_data_service.py:52-72 -- `normalize_entries` validates only name-non-empty, name-unique, value-numeric, unit-string; there is no check that the name is one the deviation engine can rule on.
findings.suggested_fix: Assumption: free-form keys are intentional (the SPEC's design-value source is still an open decision, so a hard allow-list would block legitimate interim data), and the missing piece is discoverability rather than validation. Cheapest defensible improvement, no server behaviour change: expose the rule set as a read endpoint or fold it into an existing meta endpoint -- e.g. `GET /api/v1/equipment/deviation-rules` returning each rule's `parameter` name, `design_key`, `spec_ref`, and unit -- so a client can populate the entry form from the contract instead of typing free-text Chinese parameter names. Pair that with a `description` on `ActualDataEntry.name` naming the rule endpoint. Stronger alternative if the rules are considered stable: reject unknown names at write time with a new `PcsError` (code, e.g. `ACTUAL_DATA_UNKNOWN_PARAMETER`, status 422) -- note this needs the raise inlined so `_scan_error_codes` registers the code, per the sibling finding. Do not tighten the key type without a decision on where design values come from.

findings.title: DeviationRowOut.design_value is a three-way union (number | string | null) with no discriminator for which case applies
findings.why_it_matters: The generator emits `design_value: number | string | null` into the frontend's TypeScript types, so a client that formats or does arithmetic on the design value (the obvious use in a deviation report -- percent difference against `actual_value`) compiles cleanly and then throws at runtime on the string case. The three cases mean different things -- null is 'no design value recorded' (which the engine maps to `UNVERDICTABLE`), a number is a comparable design value, and a string is a non-numeric design specification -- but the response carries no field saying which one applies, so the client must infer it from the sibling `verdict`, and only for the null case. The union is not modelling a real requirement: it exists because the service extractor is typed `-> tuple[object, str, bool]`, so anything read out of the JSONB column passes through.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/schemas/supplier.py:80 -- `design_value: float | str | None = Field(description="设计值")`

pcs-frontend/src/types/api.d.ts:7125 -- `design_value: number | string | null;` -- the generated client type, confirmed byte-identical to the backend OpenAPI (both files sha256 `30910d7b53586004`, `ja == jb` is True), so the union really does reach the frontend.

pcs-backend/app/schemas/supplier.py:81 -- `actual_value: float | str | None = Field(description="实际值")` -- the same union on the sibling field; in practice `actual_value` is always a float because `ActualDataEntry.value` is strictly `float` (schemas/supplier.py:23) and `normalize_entries` rejects non-numerics, so the string case is unreachable for actual and only theoretical for design.

pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/deviation_report.py:62 -- `def _extract(container: dict | None, name: str) -> tuple[object, str, bool]:` -- the `object` return type is what forces the union into the public schema; `_extract` returns `entry.get("value")` from an untyped JSONB column (line 70).

pcs-backend/app/schemas/supplier.py:83 -- `deviation_pct: float | None = Field(default=None, description="偏差 %; 不可判时 null")` -- by contrast this field documents what its null means; `design_value`'s null carries no such note, and the description is the bare string `"设计值"`.
findings.suggested_fix: Assumption: the design-value column is expected to hold numbers whenever a comparison is attempted -- the engine's own rules are numeric (deviation_service computes `{g}%` ratios and `deviation_pct`), and the only reason a string can appear today is the untyped JSONB extractor. Tighten the public type to `float | None` and coerce/reject at the service boundary in `_extract`: if a design value is present but non-numeric, keep the row but set `design_value=None` and `verdict=UNVERDICTABLE` with a note -- the engine already has exactly that fail-closed path at deviation_report.py:104-112 ('缺设计值，无法判定'). That makes the string case unreachable rather than merely undocumented, and lets the client treat the field as numeric-or-absent. If non-numeric design specs are a genuine requirement, keep the union but add a `design_value_kind: Literal["numeric", "text", "missing"]` discriminator to `DeviationRowOut` and extend the `design_value` description to state which case each value implies.

findings.title: actual_data_status is a bare untyped string with no description naming its four states, unlike every sibling status field in the codebase
findings.why_it_matters: The generated TypeScript is `actual_data_status: string` with no enumeration hint, so a client hardcodes the four state strings with nothing in the contract to point at. Every comparable status field in the existing schema set carries a `Field(..., description=...)` that names its states, so the new response drops the only in-band signal a client has. This matters more than usual here because the state machine is a live gate on three of the six new endpoints -- confirm is refused unless the row is past the lock, PUT is refused once CONFIRMED -- so a client that guesses a state name wrong gets a 422 whose meaning it cannot interpret.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/schemas/supplier.py:43 -- `actual_data_status: str` -- no `Field(...)`, no description, no Literal; also repeated at schemas/supplier.py:100 in `DeviationReportOut`.

pcs-backend/app/models/enums.py:178-187 -- `class ActualDataStatus(str, enum.Enum):` with `NOT_ENTERED = "NOT_ENTERED"` / `PENDING_CONFIRM = "PENDING_CONFIRM"` / `CONFIRMED = "CONFIRMED"` / `NEED_RECALC = "NEED_RECALC"` -- four states that the contract never surfaces to the client.

Convention comparison: `grep -rn 'status: str' app/schemas/*.py` shows every sibling documents its states in the description -- `app/schemas/config.py:36: status: str = Field(..., description="资产状态（DRAFT/PENDING/APPROVED/PUBLISHED/OBSOLETE）")`, `app/schemas/checklist.py:76: status: str = Field(..., description="校验状态 5 态")`, `app/schemas/cool_tower.py:284: sign_status: str = Field(..., description="签审状态 9 态")`, `app/schemas/equip_list.py:112: equipment_status: str`.
pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/actual_data_service.py:92-100 -- the CONFIRMED lock raises `code="ACTUAL_DATA_LOCKED"` 422, so a client misreading the state string is not merely cosmetic.
findings.suggested_fix: Assumption: the project convention is a documented `str` rather than a `Literal`/`Enum` in the response schema (all six sibling status fields use `str`), so match the convention rather than introducing a new pattern. Add `Field(..., description="录入状态（NOT_ENTERED/PENDING_CONFIRM/CONFIRMED/NEED_RECALC）")` to `ActualDataResponse.actual_data_status` and the same description to `DeviationReportOut.actual_data_status`. Re-run the G-08 OpenAPI contract gate afterwards to regenerate `openapi.json`, `openapi.snapshot.json`, and `api.d.ts` -- the pre-commit hook fails on drift, so the regen is mandatory, not optional. If the four states are considered stable, promoting both fields to a shared `ActualDataStatusLiteral = Literal["NOT_ENTERED", "PENDING_CONFIRM", "CONFIRMED", "NEED_RECALC"]` would give the client compile-time exhaustiveness; that is a larger change and would also require a decision on whether the enum should become a proper response model, so it is the follow-up, not the fix.

residual_risks: Verdict-tier drift is a latent 500, not a current bug. `Verdict` is declared as `Literal["QUALIFIED","WARNING","UNQUALIFIED","UNVERDICTABLE"]` in app/schemas/supplier.py:73, duplicating four bare string constants in app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py:28-31. The label/colour maps are safe from drift because `DeviationRow.label` / `.color` are `@property` delegating to `verdict_label` / `verdict_color` (deviation_report.py:40-46), so `verdict` is the single source and the client never has to string-compare. The exposure is one-directional: if a fifth tier is added to the engine, `verdict_label`'s `.get(verdict, "不可判")` fallback silently returns the UNVERDICTABLE label, but `DeviationRowOut.model_validate` at supplier.py:136 rejects the unknown tier first, so the read endpoint returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR rather than degrading. I did not raise this as a finding because no fifth tier exists today; the schema Literal is the tripwire and it is in the right place, it just fails closed rather than open. Worth a regression test if a tier is ever added.

I did not reach the frontend UI-SPEC conformance check. CLAUDE.md names `docs/PCS-UI-SPEC.md` (V1.0 frozen) as the sole encoding basis for frontend UI, and I confirmed no frontend component consumes the six new endpoints yet, so there is nothing yet to check for conformance -- but that check becomes live as soon as the S4 UI lands.

The export endpoint is clean on the points asked about. `format` is constrained by `Query(pattern="^(excel|pdf)")` (supplier.py:223), so an invalid value produces a FastAPI `RequestValidationError` -> 422 `VALIDATION_ERROR` in the standard envelope, not a 500. `Content-Type` is drawn from `_EXPORT_TYPES` and `Content-Disposition` correctly uses RFC 5987 `filename*=UTF-8''` with the tag number percent-encoded via `quote(..., safe="")` (supplier.py:241-251), so Chinese tag numbers survive. No finding.

Error-shape consistency is clean and I checked it rather than assuming. Both failure modes carry the same `ErrorResponse` envelope with a `code` field: `PcsError` routes through the `_service_pcs` handler, FastAPI validation failures through the `_validation` handler (`code="VALIDATION_ERROR"`, app/core/errors.py), and bare `HTTPException` through the Starlette handler (`code=f"HTTP_{exc.status_code}"`). The new endpoints' `HTTPException(404, ...)` in `_load_equipment` is the established project pattern -- `_guard.check_project_access_or_404` and `config.py::_load_asset` do the same. A client parses one shape, not two. One consequence the author chose deliberately: not-found and no-access both collapse to `HTTP_404`, which is correct for not leaking existence but does mean a 404 from these endpoints is ambiguous by design.

OpenAPI regeneration is verifiably correct. `pcs-backend/docs/openapi.json` and `pcs-frontend/openapi.snapshot.json` are byte-identical (both sha256 `30910d7b53586004`, `json.loads(a) == json.loads(b)` is True), and the document contains exactly 196 paths including all five new ones with the expected methods. The G-08 gate's three `chore(p7-s4): regen OpenAPI 契约` commits are not drift. No finding.

The frontend mock error-code seed (pcs-frontend/src/mocks/seed/meta.ts) has zero `ACTUAL_DATA_*` entries, so even after the backend registry is fixed the mock layer would not serve the new codes. I did not make this a finding because that seed carries only 36 of the backend's 115 codes and is a hand-maintained subset, so the gap is pre-existing and broader than this branch -- but it means a fix to finding #1 will not be observable in mock-mode development until the seed is separately extended.
testing_gaps: No test asserts that the error codes emitted by the new endpoints are present in the /api/v1/meta/error-codes response. This is precisely the gap that let `ACTUAL_DATA_VALIDATION` and `DEVIATION_BLOCKS_CONFIRMATION` ship unregistered: tests/api/v1/test_supplier_actual_data_api.py:156 asserts the code is *emitted* but nothing cross-checks it is *catalogued*. A single test that calls the meta endpoint and asserts every code raised by the supplier service modules appears in it would close the class, not just this instance.

No test pins the route prefix against the SPEC. Nothing in the suite would have failed on the /equipment vs /equipment-list divergence. A lightweight guard that reads the SPEC API table and asserts each documented path resolves in the app's route table would make the SPEC/OpenAPI drift from finding #2 mechanically detectable instead of relying on a human noticing.

No test exercises an unknown parameter name end-to-end. The `rule is None` -> UNVERDICTABLE branch at deviation_report.py:93-100 has no service-level test that writes a free-form key through PUT and reads back a UNVERDICTABLE row, so the write-surface/read-surface asymmetry in finding #3 is currently asserted only at the unit level (if at all).

No test covers the `design_value` string case. The `float | str | None` union is never exercised with a non-numeric design value, so the runtime type hazard in finding #4 is untested in either direction -- neither proven reachable nor proven unreachable.
